findings.problem: Verdict "no-bonus" discards a printed typed bonus. The text plainly prints "+2 status bonus to saves against poison and charm effects" under the Unicorn option. Their argument ("the bonus belongs to the stored choice, not the feat record") is a design claim, not a text claim, and it is contradicted by the registry's own house style, which routinely encodes choose-one-of-N bonuses by naming the option inside `when` — e.g. mutate-weapon ("only if you chose the attack-bonus option instead of 10-foot reach"), bloodline-demonic / bloodline-diabolic / bloodline-aesir ("if you choose the self-benefit of ... instead of ..."). Their stated risk ("shows a bonus most owners of the feat do not have") is exactly what the trigger field prevents, and the star lane is display-only, so nothing in the total can be inflated. Dropping it means an Anteater/Unicorn player never sees a rule the book prints.

extracted.action: Make an Impression or a Request (when negotiating a deal or agreement)
extracted.reason: Make an Impression and Request are Diplomacy actions, and this feat adds Legal Lore as a second skill that can perform them while negotiating. But the bonus is NOT attached to the action generally — "these checks" are the checks just described, i.e. the Legal-Lore-in-place-of-Diplomacy ones. Foundry's rule element agrees: selector `legal-lore`, predicated on action:make-an-impression / action:request, with the value scaling off skill:diplomacy:rank. So the only skill that can carry the bonus is Legal Lore; Diplomacy can still perform the action but gets nothing, and starring it would invent a bonus the text does not grant. Diplomacy proficiency only sets the SIZE of the bonus. Answering the open question: (a) the registry key is `lore:legal` — build.ts keys lores as lore:<subject> with the trailing " Lore" stripped, lowercased and hyphenated (matching lore:games, lore:warfare, lore:fortune-telling already in the file); (b) show the whole ladder as text, since the star is display-only and must not recompute — the house style already does this ("+1 to +4 item (by grade)").
extracted.quote: When negotiating deals or agreements, you can use Legal Lore in place of Diplomacy to Make an Impression or a Request, even if there is no legal framework under which you are negotiating. If you are an expert in Diplomacy, you gain a +1 circumstance bonus to these checks; if you are a master in Diplomacy, this increases to +2, and +3 if you are legendary.

situational.when: to Make an Impression or a Request while negotiating a deal or agreement, using Legal Lore in place of Diplomacy
situational.bonus: +1 circumstance if expert in Diplomacy, +2 if master, +3 if legendary

extracted.action: document or reproduce carved, etched, or physically added artwork or writing
extracted.reason: Answering the open question: skill:'all' with the condition text, NOT a narrowing to Crafting and Society. "Checks to document or reproduce" is not a codified PF2e action with a published skill list — there is no Document action, and Craft, Decipher Writing and Recall Knowledge are all different things — so there is no rules basis for saying which skills can and cannot be rolled. Every other record here narrows because the action itself names its skills (Earn Income lists three, Identify Magic lists four); this one names none, so ruling out Society, Thievery, Art Lore, Architecture Lore or anything else would be inventing a restriction the text does not support. Starring all skills with the trigger spelled out is the only faithful encoding: the star never changes a number, so the cost of the wide net is only that the note appears on more stats, whereas narrowing would silently hide a bonus the player is entitled to. Note the +1 is consumed on use (the kit is expended), which the trigger records.
extracted.quote: Using the kit consumes the materials and provides a +1 item bonus on checks to document or reproduce artwork or writing that has been carved, etched, or otherwise physically added to a surface.

situational.when: on checks to document or reproduce artwork or writing that has been carved, etched, or otherwise physically added to a surface (using the kit consumes it)

extracted.action: Investigate a crime scene, a clue, or similar details
extracted.reason: The text names no skill at all — it ties the bonus to the TASK of investigating, which in PF2e has no fixed skill. Seeking the scene for physical evidence is Perception; the kit's own contents map onto several different skills (vials and tweezers = Crafting/Medicine on a body or a substance, calipers and knotted string = Society or Crafting for measurements, chalk and notebook = Society/Thievery for reconstructing a break-in, plus any relevant Lore). Because the printed trigger is a task and not an action with a published skill list, the only honest expansion under the ruling is Perception plus skill 'all' — 'every skill that could do it' here really is any skill the GM allows for that investigation. I deliberately do NOT narrow it to a short list, because the text gives no basis for excluding any particular skill.

situational.when: to investigate a crime scene, a clue, or similar details, while carrying the kit

extracted.action: Recall Knowledge to identify an elemental creature
extracted.reason: Identifying a creature is Recall Knowledge, and the skill is set by the creature's type. Elemental appears on the Recall Knowledge creature table under Arcana and Nature — those are the two core skills that can identify an elemental, and no others (Occultism and Religion cover different types, Society covers humanoids, Crafting covers constructs). A relevant Lore (Elemental Lore, Plane of Fire Lore, etc.) can always substitute for a Recall Knowledge check, so lore:* is included; the trigger keeps it honest by naming the subject, so only a Lore about elementals actually qualifies.

The second half says only 'skill checks', naming no skill: working out why a haunt or a spirit persists is Recall Knowledge about a haunt (an occult hazard, identified with Occultism) or about an undead/spirit-trait entity (identified with Religion for undead, Occultism for the spirit trait) — those two are the skills that can perform it. findings.problem: INVENTED RESTRICTION / WRONG SKILL SET. The printed text never says the check to identify celestial bodies is a Survival check. What it says is 'To use an astrolabe, the holder must be trained in Survival' — that is a training gate on operating the item, not the skill the check is rolled with. The encoder converted that gate into 'Survival is the identifying skill' and then used it to EXCLUDE every other skill. Nothing in the text supports the exclusion: 'checks to identify celestial bodies' names no skill at all, and there is no published action or creature-type table that assigns celestial bodies to Survival (Sense Direction is navigation, not identifying a star). Concrete omissions caused by the narrowing: Occultism (astrology/esoterica is squarely occult), Nature, Arcana, and every Lore other than Astronomy — none of which the text excludes. findings.problem: Two defects. (1) LOST RESTRICTION: the printed sentence opens 'When you carry or wield a gravedigger's call...', and that condition governs BOTH halves of the bonus. The encoder kept it on the Perception entry ('while carrying or wielding the shovel') but dropped it entirely from the second entry, whose `when` is just 'to determine the reasons for a haunt or spirit's existence' — as written that star would show even with the shovel left at home, and it contradicts the encoder's own first entry. (2) INVENTED RESTRICTION / WRONG SKILL SET: the text says 'skill checks', naming no skill; narrowing that to Occultism + Religion excludes Society (researching a cemetery's or a family's history to learn why a spirit lingers) and every other skill the text does not exclude. This is also internally inconsistent with the same encoder's detectives-kit record, where an equally skill-less trigger ('investigate a crime scene, a clue, or similar details') was correctly given skill 'all'; and with house precedent spirit-walk (src/rules/situationalBonuses.ts line 558), which encodes 'Recall Knowledge checks about spirits, haunts, and undead' as skill 'all'. Corrected: keep Perception-only for the explicitly-Perception half, use skill 'all' for the 'skill checks' half, and restore the carry/wield condition on both. The bonus value and type (+1 item) were right and are unchanged.
